newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close lower after wide fluctuations.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close lower after wide fluctuations.

text.p: Stocks ended lower on Wednesday after wide fluctuations in a tug of war between bargain hunting and profit taking, brokers said.
Trading was delayed by 30 minutes on Wednesday due to the first round of university entrance exams.
"Trading was volatile. Bargain hunting struggled with profit taking throughout the day," said Kim Heung-shik, a broker at Hyundai Securities.
The composite index provisionally ended 5.22 points lower at 747.32. It moved in 743.71-757.72 range. Brokers said hopes of state boosting steps supported the market in early afternoon.
Volume totalled 23.19 million shares, compared with 28.09 million on Tuesday.
Losers outpaced gainers 572 to 319 with 117 unchanged.

Rumours said the government was considering steps including cuting securities transactions tax, providing tax incentives to long-term stockholders and increasing the return on customer deposits at brokerage houses, brokers said.

Brokers saw the market moving in a range from 720 to 770 for the rest of the month. Samsung Electronics, which gained sharply on Tuesday on an improved semiconductor book-to-bill ratio, lost 1,700 won to 65,200 won.
"Investors turned jittery again. Factors like an oversupply of stocks are still weighing on the market," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
Shares of Sunkyong Group companies fell despite the group's announcement of higher 1997 sales targets.
Sungkyong Ltd, a trading arm of the group, lost 200 won to 13,200, while Yukong Ltd, a refining company, dropped 400 won to 19,400.
The group said on Wednesday its sales target for next year was set at 36 trillion won, up from 31 trillion for this year.
